title: categorical

gpu_support.notes: Categorical arrays are host metadata objects.

description: `categorical(A)` maps input labels to integer category codes and stores category labels in object metadata.
behaviors: String, char, cellstr, numeric, and logical inputs are supported.
`categorical(A)` derives sorted unique categories from non-missing labels.
String labels preserve leading and trailing whitespace.
`categorical(A, valueset)` uses the supplied values as the category order and marks unmatched labels as missing.
`categorical(A, valueset, catnames)` maps source values through `valueset` and stores the corresponding category names from `catnames`; `valueset` entries must be unique.
Empty labels become missing category codes.
`"Ordinal"` and `"Protected"` are accepted as name-value options, while those same words can still be used as positional category labels when not followed by logical option values.
Categorical-to-categorical comparisons require matching category lists.
Ordinal categorical arrays support equality, relational comparisons, `min`, and `max` by category order.
Use `ordinal(...)` as a compatibility constructor for categoricals whose category order is meaningful.
